```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(varm)
set.seed(1)
```

## What is implemented

This table was compiled from the package source (`R/`, `src/*.cpp`), not from
the package description. Items marked "not yet" appear in the `DESCRIPTION`,
`_pkgdown.yml` or notes but have no code.

| Area | Implemented | Entry point |
|---|---|---|
| Reduced-form VAR | OLS with constant, linear trend, exogenous regressors; lag selection (AIC, HQ, SC, FPE); `summary`, `coef`, `resid`, `fitted`, `vcov`, `logLik`; companion-matrix stability | `varm()`, `var_select()`, `stability()` |
| Uncertainty | residual bootstrap, wild bootstrap (Rademacher, Mammen), asymptotic Monte Carlo, Kilian bias correction | `draws()`, `irf(ci = )` |
| Dynamics | IRFs (with bands, normalisation, cumulation), FEVD, historical decomposition, forecasts with bands | `irf()`, `fevd()`, `hd()`, `forecast()` |
| SVAR identification | Cholesky, Blanchard-Quah long-run, sign restrictions (Haar rotations), user-supplied impact matrix | `id_chol()`, `id_longrun()`, `id_sign()`, `id_given()` |
| Bayesian VAR | conjugate Normal-inverse-Wishart with Minnesota, sum-of-coefficients and single-unit-root priors; exact sampling for fixed hyperparameters, Metropolis for hierarchical hyperparameters | `bvarm()`, `prior_minnesota()` |
| Proxy SVAR | in progress | |
| Not yet | external-instrument/proxy (in progress), heteroskedasticity identification, narrative/zero restrictions, stochastic volatility, shrinkage (SSVS) priors, TVP-VAR, FAVAR, local projections, data simulation helper | |

The `_pkgdown.yml` reference index also lists `favar`, `autoplot.varm`,
`autolayer.varm` and `sim_var`; none of these exist in the code.

## Data

`yraw` holds three quarterly US series (columns `X1`-`X3`: inflation,
unemployment and the interest rate in the Koop-Korobilis data set). We rename
them and drop the tibble class.

```{r data}
y <- as.matrix(yraw)
colnames(y) <- c("inflation", "unemployment", "rate")
y <- ts(y, start = 1953, frequency = 4)
dim(y)
```

## Lag selection and estimation

```{r select}
var_select(y, pmax = 6)$selection
fit <- varm(y, p = 2)
fit
```

```{r summary}
summary(fit)
stability(fit)   # moduli of companion eigenvalues, all < 1 for a stationary VAR
```

`coef(fit)` returns the `(Kp + d) x K` coefficient matrix (lags first, then
deterministic terms); `lag_matrices(fit)` returns the `K x K x p` array of
lag matrices.

```{r lags}
round(lag_matrices(fit)[, , 1], 3)
```

## Impulse responses

`irf()` defaults to a Cholesky identification and a residual bootstrap. The
result stores the point estimate in `$estimate` (response x shock x horizon)
and bands in `$bands`.

```{r irf}
ir <- irf(fit, id = id_chol(), horizon = 16, nboot = 300)
ir
dim(ir$estimate)
```

Use `ci = "none"` for point estimates only, or `"wild"`, `"wild_mammen"`,
`"mc"` for the other draw generators. `normalise` rescales a shock (here a
unit shock to the rate), and `cumulative` accumulates responses of variables
entered in differences.

```{r irf-opts}
ir_wild <- irf(fit, horizon = 16, ci = "wild", nboot = 300,
               normalise = list(shock = "rate", variable = "rate", size = 1))
```

## Plotting

`plot()` on an IRF or FEVD object draws a response-by-shock grid. The return
value depends on the installed version (base graphics or ggplot2), so the
code below only calls `plot()` and the optional subsetting arguments.

```{r plot, fig.height = 4}
plot(ir, shocks = "rate")
```

`as.data.frame()` gives a tidy table for your own plots.

```{r tidy}
head(as.data.frame(ir), 4)
```

## FEVD, historical decomposition and forecasts

```{r fevd}
fv <- fevd(fit, horizon = 12, ci = "none")
round(fv$estimate[, , 13], 3)    # response x shock at horizon 12
```

```{r hd}
h <- hd(fit)
dim(h$contributions)             # time x variable x shock
```

```{r fc}
fc <- forecast(fit, h = 8, nboot = 300)
fc
dim(fc$bands)                    # horizon x variable x probability
```
